releases.body:
# Test build for no audio on some PCs (#1165)

This build is for players who have no sound at all on 3.0.0, with `No default audio device available` in `user/last_run.log`. It is not a final release.

## What changes

- When Windows reports no default audio device and SDL gives no driver name, the game now tries DirectSound before it goes silent. Before, that fallback only ran when the driver was named WASAPI.
- Everything else is 3.0.0.

## How to test

1. Copy your save folder first.
2. Extract `spartanport-windows.zip` into a **new folder**, so your current install stays as it is.
3. Start the game and check whether the intro and the gameplay have sound.
4. Reply on #1165 with **sound** or **still silent**, plus your `user/last_run.log`.

## Validation

- The new audio test failed before the fix and passes after it, together with the existing WASAPI fallback, forced driver and total failure tests, and the downmix test (MSYS2 CLANG64, warnings as errors).
- Built and opened on a clean Windows runner by the release workflow.
- Not checked in game: we could not reproduce a PC with no default audio device.

> **SpartanPort 3.0.0: the launcher is now Rust, with no Python.** Updating from 2.7.0 through the launcher keeps your saves and settings. These notes cover the 27 pull requests merged since 2.7.0, through `a2299cd` (#1150), including the version bump to 3.0.0. 2.8.0 was never published: its launcher work ships here.

## Updating from 2.7.0

- **Windows:** update through the launcher as usual. The 2.7.0 launcher downloads 3.0.0 and the new launcher installs itself over the old folder. Saves, `user/`, `spartanport.ini`, launcher settings, mods, patches and `last_run.log` are not touched. - **Linux:** download `spartanport-x86_64.AppImage` from this release and replace the old file. The launcher keeps offering updates from here on.
- **Settings carried over:** the launcher imports your previous settings. Shader notes in the corner stay **off**, and the new **High FPS Wall Seam Fix** patch is ticked once in a saved patch list; untick it and it stays unticked.

# Test build 2 for infinite loading screens (#1131)

This build is for players stuck on a loading screen that never ends. It is not a final release: it tells us whether fixes that are not in 2.7.0 yet remove the hang, and if not, where the load stops.

## What changes

- **Memory fixes from #1005**, already on `main` but in no release yet. Among them, copy threads now read guest memory through a second view, so they no longer wait on a GPU thread that waits on them.
- **Texture cache, GPU and shader cache fixes from #1124.** On graphics cards with less than 8 GB, texture pressure now starts at 60% of the budget instead of about 40%, the collector no longer gets stuck behind images it must keep, and an old "GPU idle" signal can no longer release newer work.

releases.name: v0.2.1: All treat, no trick! 🎃
releases.body:
Hi everyone! I'm happy to announce a new release, two months after the previous one. 

Before I get to the changelog, some special notes:

- From this release onwards, the old list of supported apps is replaced by the new, crowdsourced [touchHLE app compatibility database](https://appdb.touchhle.org/).
- In case you missed it, the [touchHLE app archive](https://touchhle.org/app-archive/) was recently launched. It only has one app at the moment, but that's hopefully just the start. If you were an indie developer in the early iPhone days, please get in touch!
- If you want to get notified about future releases, you might want to join the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/sVMXc8z3eS). You can't post there, but you'll be @'d with updates. There's also a [YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@touchHLE) where I post short gameplay videos with new releases.
- If you want to help me keep working on this full time, please consider [supporting me financially](https://liberapay.com/hikari_no_yume).

Finally, a big thanks to all the other contributors who made this release what it was! If it weren't for them, there might not have been any new game support in this release.

Happy Hallowee

This release candidate fixes an audio-update parsing error that could cause invalid mixer data and audio glitches.

**This is a pre-release for testing before v0.1.1.** Feedback and reproducible bug reports are welcome. It includes all improvements from rc1 through rc5.

### What’s new since rc5

- **Audio update parsing:** the audio renderer now respects the splitter block size declared in the update header. Previously, it could read the following mixer block at the wrong offset, resulting in invalid mix counts or rejected audio updates.
- **Input validation:** added bounds checks for declared splitter blocks.
- **Regression coverage:** added synthetic tests covering splitter block boundaries, subsequent mixer updates, and header layout.

This correction addresses a likely cause of the audio errors reported in [issue #21](https://github.com/vricosti/ruzu-emu/issues/21). Confirmation through extended gameplay is still needed.

### Known limitations

Unsupported shader instructions may still cause missing graphics or prevent a scene from rendering. This release does not resolve every freeze, black-screen issue, or audio glitch.

Multi-program game compatibility remains experimental.

## Hollow Knight: Silksong Android 2.0.0-rc1

**Note when updating from a previous version**: This will trigger the porting process again, but it is heavily cached, so should only take a few minutes.

## Hollow Knight: Silksong Android 2.0.0

**Note when updating from a previous version**: This will trigger the porting process again, but it is heavily cached, so should only take a few minutes.

This is a major release for this project, where the biggest change is that we have completely redesigned the bottom screen UI to feel more native to Silksongs design language. The bottom screen UI should now feel familiar to anyone who has used the in-game menu and any action can be taken from the bottom screen menu, making the in-game menu obsolete.

Thanks to Kaz Kirigiri for doing most of the design work and providing sketches for this revamped UI!

## Changes since 1.1.0

### Completely revamped bottom screen UI

- All tabs have been revamped to follow the in-game menu as close as possible
- Every action from the menu can now be done from the bottom screen. Use items, change crest and tools, place markers
- Smoothly animated item selection, tab switching, etc

## Changes since 2.0.0-rc1

### Dual screen
  - Zoom slider on the map: drag up to zoom in, down to zoom out. Fades out like RESET when you're not touching the map
  - Equipping and unequipping tools is animated: the tool flies

releases.body:
Fixes the device-specific startup crash caused by an outdated or mismatched support archive.

Highlights:
- Verifies the installed support archive against the APK and repairs it safely when needed
- Confirms the required OpenGL shader is present before startup
- Tries one recovery launch without mods after a native startup failure
- Preserves the selected Android menu scale between launches
- Adds clearer native crash details for shader and startup failures

Crash reports remain local and are never uploaded automatically.

releases.body:
### Fixed

- Frame captures (`RPS5E_CAPTURE_FRAMES`) of GTA V replay again instead of hanging the GPU. While a capture recorded, GPU results copied straight into guest memory were later taken for CPU writes and recorded; the replay wrote them over its own GPU results, which differ where GPU work orders its atomics differently, and the mixed ray-tracing tree sent a shader into an endless loop. releases.body:
### Added

- Games run straight from disk images of game dumps, without extracting them: exFAT images (`.exfat`, also inside an MBR or GPT partition), `.ffpfsc` containers (a PS5 PFS image holding a compressed exFAT image) and UFS2 images (`.ffpkg` dumps made on the console). The game folder is found anywhere inside the image.

releases.name: 0.1.1-alpha
releases.body:
### Added

- Display resolution setting (720p, 1080p or 2160p) in the launcher, the "Run with..." dialog, `--display-resolution` and `RPS5E_DISPLAY_RESOLUTION`: games that ask the console for the TV's resolution are told the chosen one, as a PS5 on that TV would answer; the default stays 2160p.
- PlayGo: `scePlayGoRequestOptionalChunk`, `scePlayGoGetRequiredDisc`, `scePlayGoRequestNextChunk`, `scePlayGoSnapshot` and `scePlayGoSetInstallSpeed2` are implemented. The library now tracks its initialized and open-handle state (`NOT_INITIALIZED`, `ALREADY_INITIALIZED`, `BAD_HANDLE` after close), remembers the install speed that was set, and answers a chunk-id count query made without a list buffer.

### Performance

- GTA V in the city: the longest stalls are much shorter (about 2.5 s instead of 10 s) and driving stutters far less. The frame rate in the city is still low (about 7 fps now that the ray-traced reflections are drawn) and far from playable.
- Wave64 compute shaders on 32-wide GPUs (NVIDIA): lane stacks and register spills stay in registers, ballots share one exchange, and programs from 16 VGPRs run split; the ray traversal of GTA V takes about a third of its former GPU time.
